answer: Think of one device cluster opening N accounts. Rule: account k from a cluster locks a pigment deposit of 5*2^(k-1) POA for 25 epochs. N=1 costs 5; N=10 costs 5*(2^10-1)=5,115; N=20 costs 5,242,875, and deposits cannot be shared across accounts. A prism group of 3 auditors samples 1 in 12 new accounts per epoch, compares device and timing traces, and posts matches in the grove log. An honest user with one account locks 5 POA once and gets it back. A wrongly clustered user appeals within 6 epochs for a refund. It fails if attackers rent thousands of separate devices.
